biography.plain_text: Robert “Robin” Briggs is a British marine-services entrepreneur, founder and group chairman of Burntisland-based Briggs Marine. He established the family-owned business in 1972 to supply workboats for coastal construction, then expanded it into environmental response, port operations, subsea services and vessel management. Briggs remains the majority controller while his son Collieson serves as managing director.

long_biography.plain_text:
An oil-spill response vessel changed the direction of Robert “Robin” Briggs’s Scottish marine business in 1987. The investment created Briggs Environmental Services and placed the company on response teams after the Piper Alpha disaster and the Exxon Valdez spill. The move added environmental capability to the workboat operation Briggs had developed around the Firth of Forth.

Technical diversification continued under his chairmanship. The group moved into heavy moorings, navigation aids, port management and subsea cable work. It became responsible for Ministry of Defence moorings and aids around the United Kingdom, Gibraltar and Cyprus. Briggs also co-invented a cable-handling vehicle assigned to the company, reflecting his continuing engagement with marine engineering.
